title: PhysicsRigidBodyAPI
summary: Makes an Xformable prim a rigid body. Enumerated by usd-schemas CONTAINS PhysicsRigidBodyAPI. Colliders are the prim itself if it is a Gprim with PhysicsCollisionAPI, plus descendant Gprims with PhysicsCollisionAPI.
producer_scope: Every declared attribute is published at its resolved value; relationships only when authored (an authored empty target list is an empty row). The producer also resolves the physics material binding onto this prim (see MaterialBindingAPI) and creates five units-aware PhysxRigidBodyAPI columns when they are unauthored, whether or not PhysxRigidBodyAPI is applied (see that component).

columns.name: physics:rigidBodyEnabled

verify.notes: No sample: a static body invalidates every body-targeted check.

columns.absent: Dynamic body. False produces a static body that ignores every PhysxRigidBodyAPI column.

columns.name: physics:kinematicEnabled

verify.notes: No sample: kinematic plus a non-zero velocity sample would promote the body to a surface-velocity body.

columns.absent: Not kinematic. A kinematic body with a non-zero velocity is promoted to a surface-velocity body.

verify.notes: No sample: an authored velocity in the same test would legitimately wake the body. Simulation state, compared between the two population paths only: PhysX puts a kinematic body with no target to sleep after the first step (isSleeping true on the conveyor_cube composition although startsAsleep is absent), and a dynamic body may fall asleep later, so the value after one step is not the authored flag.

columns.name: physics:velocity

verify.notes: Simulation state: observed after one step, so gravity, damping and locked axes have already acted on it. Compared between population paths only.

columns.notes: Stored USD-native. Neither the producer nor the consumer converts units; the consumer rotates into world space only when localSpaceVelocities is true.

columns.name: physics:angularVelocity
columns.notes: Stored in degrees per second as USD declares it; the consumer converts to radians.

columns.name: usd-metadata:customData:physics:localSpaceVelocities

producer.writes: the nested customData value physics -> localSpaceVelocities when present on any prim the physics selector matched
producer.notes: A flat customData key spelled "physics:localSpaceVelocities" is unaddressable by USD and is never published. When the key is removed the producer deletes the column; publishing false is not a substitute.

columns.absent: Velocities are interpreted per the consumer-wide setting. When true, the linear velocity is multiplied by the prim's decomposed world scale in local axes, then both velocities are rotated into world space, at load and on supported later edits. On a PointInstancer prototype the same rule governs the instancer's `velocities` and `angularVelocities` arrays: each is rotated into that instance's own world frame, and the linear one is scaled by the instancer's decomposed world scale -- the per-instance `scales` entry and the prototype's own scale do not take part -- see [Local-space instance velocities](../simulation_setup/rigid_bodies.md#local-space-instance-velocities). After the scene's first DirectGPU step, live ovstage velocity edits do not update dynamic (non-kinematic) bodies; use world-space session writes instead, with angular velocity in rad/s rather than the USD deg/s. Articulation roots and links are out of scope: a root is reframed at load but a live velocity edit is applied raw (and, on a DirectGPU scene after its first step, not at all), so drive it with the world-space root-velocity session write instead. See [limitations](../read_write/limitations.md).

columns.name: physics:simulationOwner
columns.absent: Body joins the default scene. A non-empty list whose targets resolve to no PhysicsScene drops the body.
columns.notes: Path-dictionary ids in USD target order. Present only when authored; an authored empty list is an empty row.

interactions.rule: World translation and rotation, composed from omni:xform up the chain (or omni:fabric:worldMatrix when present), become the initial body pose. Later world-matrix-only edits do not trigger a physics transform update; see [Transform inputs](../ovstage_integration.md#transform-inputs).
No scene relationship is required; see PhysicsScene for the consumer's synthetic default.

The producer creates sleepThreshold, stabilizationThreshold, maxDepenetrationVelocity, maxLinearVelocity and maxContactImpulse columns on every rigid body when unauthored. Without PhysxRigidBodyAPI in usd-schemas the consumer ignores them.

notes: The dynamic-body scalar batch also requests physxSplinesSurfaceVelocity:surfaceVelocityEnabled and :surfaceVelocityMagnitude for every dynamic body, applied API or not; the values are used only when PhysxSplinesSurfaceVelocityAPI is listed. That component owns the columns; the compiled cache reads them without supporting it.
